title: Completion and recentering isolate the nontrivial zero geometry
claim: Multiplying zeta by its pole- and gamma-correcting factors, folding with the functional equation, and then writing s=1/2+it preserves the nontrivial-zero question while replacing a meromorphic strip problem by an entire even function whose critical-line zeros are real t-roots.
historical_or_program_relation: Riemann's theta-integral split-reflect-center construction, the later explicit separation of xi zeros from gamma/pole artifacts, and the modern real-rootedness formulation are successive presentations of the same representation change and its preserved zero data.
limits: Completion proves symmetry, decay, and confinement only after analytic continuation, Euler-product nonvanishing, and the functional equation are available; evenness and reality on the line do not imply that all zeros are real or even supply an existence proof.

title: The prime-zero bridge retains prime powers and a summation prescription
claim: Logarithms and transforms turn the Euler product into an additive prime-power count, residues turn analytic singularities into a zero expansion, and Mobius inversion removes prime-power iterates only at the later prime-counting stage; because the zero expansion is conditionally convergent, contour-induced magnitude ordering is part of the representation.
historical_or_program_relation: Riemann's ordered zero sum and Mobius separation are made explicit in modern prime-zero duality accounts, which retain the weighted prime-power density as the directly reconstructible intermediate object before optionally recovering primes alone.
limits: The bridge does not make arbitrary rearrangements valid, and a finite or smoothed zero sum recovers only a resolution-limited approximation; treating prime powers as removable noise before inversion discards signal that the explicit formula naturally preserves.

title: Perron inversion trades sharp coefficient recovery for decay and resolution obligations
claim: A vertical Perron kernel converts a Dirichlet series into cumulative coefficients through residues, but a valid finite contour requires both a remainder representation with edge decay and a height budget whose truncation error grows near the cutoff discontinuity.
historical_or_program_relation: The generalized-series proof isolates decay by subtracting the pre-cutoff terms and shifting by the first surviving exponent, while the modern truncated formula exposes contour height as a frequency-resolution parameter; both refine the general Dirichlet-series-to-summatory-function bridge.
limits: The line must remain to the right of the relevant convergence boundary, the sharp cutoff has a canonical half-weight at equality, and neither the abstract inversion template nor larger height alone controls a raw remainder whose horizontal edges fail to vanish.

title: Finite RH verification composes exhaustive counts with certified line witnesses
claim: A finite-height RH certificate is obtained by matching an argument-principle total zero count to critical-line sign-change witnesses after phase normalization, while absolute error envelopes, endpoint closure, count identities, reruns, and overlapping computations protect the numerical-to-integer step.
historical_or_program_relation: The conceptual count-plus-witness certificate is refined by computational practice from Gram-point detection into explicit truncation/interpolation/arithmetic error margins and targeted reruns of known bookkeeping vulnerabilities.
limits: Gram-point sampling is not itself complete, adjacent-block recovery has a documented counterexample pattern, related program versions and machines are not independent implementations, and the conclusion is only for the certified finite rectangle.

title: Verified zeros and zero-free geometry cover complementary ranges in explicit prime bounds
claim: Finite zero verification can anchor the low-height side of an all-height zero-free inequality, while an asymptotic zero-free region controls the upper side; contour height then balances inversion error against allowable displacement to transfer the joined coverage into explicit psi, theta, and prime-counting errors.
historical_or_program_relation: The qualitative PNT contour mechanism is converted into an explicit coverage-and-optimization pipeline in which verified height, zero-free geometry, finite psi estimates, and downstream reoptimization are separate improvement levers.
limits: The splice inherits every constant, crossover, and overlap obligation of its inputs; verified RH below a height says nothing by itself above it, the levers are not interchangeable, and the resulting error remains far from the square-root scale that full RH would imply.

title: Smoothing makes zero expansions operable but changes the recovery problem
claim: Kernel smoothing and Mellin transformation replace a conditionally organized zero formula by weighted identities that permit interchange, integration, factorization, tail bounds, and transfer across weight families; this can let one low zero pair force oscillation after the remaining weighted tail is controlled.
historical_or_program_relation: The contour-prescribed ordering already present in Riemann's formula becomes an explicit regularization technology in smoothed explicit formulas and transform-Tauberian arguments, relocating the burden from formal summation to kernel choice and endpoint estimates.
limits: A smoothed oscillation result is not automatically a statement about the raw summatory error, unsmoothing requires Tauberian hypotheses, and changing the kernel or ordering changes the admissible manipulations and the quantitative tail rather than merely changing notation.

title: A spectral model must derive rather than encode the zeros
claim: Zero statistics and involutive eigenvalue pairing motivate a spectral formulation but do not supply spectral reality; a credible Hilbert-Polya mechanism must construct a zero-independent space and a legitimate common domain or geometric sign structure from which the zeros and their reality follow.
historical_or_program_relation: Random-matrix and finite-field analogies state the structural target, Connes's cokernel/support mechanism shows how zeros can emerge where an analytic multiplier fails to force density, and the proposed difference Hamiltonian exposes domain, adjoint, completeness, and self-adjointness as the unresolved decisive obligations.
limits: Connes's support classification and the formal Hamiltonian are distinct constructions and cannot be fused into one operator; PT symmetry only pairs eigenvalues, the cited statistics are motivational, and neither program as represented here proves self-adjointness or RH.

title: Universal zero statistics require a separate arithmetic factor
claim: Random-matrix characteristic polynomials can match local correlations, lower-order extreme-value behavior, and moment predictions while omitting Euler-product arithmetic; the hybrid Euler-Hadamard representation repairs that loss by assigning prime data and nearby-zero data to compensating factors whose product is stable as the cutoff changes.
historical_or_program_relation: Agreement of independently motivated moment heuristics and numerical freezing diagnostics strengthens a universality program, while the later hybrid factorization turns the known arithmetic mismatch into an explicit two-factor representation rather than an external correction constant alone.
limits: The moment agreements and freezing curve are heuristic or numerical and have slow finite-height convergence; the hybrid split is cutoff-dependent, its compensating plots are representation checks, and neither universality evidence nor factorization establishes RH or an underlying self-adjoint operator.

title: Generalization is informative only when it exposes a new invariant
claim: Embedding zeta in a larger theory can expose missing geometry, automorphy, or Hecke structure, but a componentwise bicomplex lift transports continuation and zero data through two scalar projections without adding such a mechanism; its conjunctive zero set is a Cartesian pairing, and a hyperbolic restriction collapses the nontrivial zero geometry.
historical_or_program_relation: The general L-function program uses enlargement to seek shared arithmetic or spectral invariants, whereas the bicomplex construction is a controlled counterexample to treating every formally broader zeta object as an explanatory generalization.
limits: The bicomplex continuation and reconstruction are legitimate representation transfers and are not refuted by this comparison; the point is only that component independence and zero divisors add no demonstrated route to classical RH, while membership in the broader automorphic or geometric L-function package remains difficult in its own right.

title: Family functional equations require completion of both local factors and the index set
claim: To make a family of L-functions close under reflection, one must split sign and conductor classes, attach parity-dependent gamma factors, correct imprimitive twists so dual summation orders agree, and then use a uniformly controlled Mobius sieve to recover the primitive family.
historical_or_program_relation: This realizes the general-L-function idea that a shared analytic package comes from arithmetic structure: completion advances from a single-function involution to a finite-dimensional system of commuting family involutions, with correction polynomials and sieving carrying the new proof burden.
limits: The initial completed family symmetry does not by itself continue to the averaging pole or prove a moment theorem; correction uniqueness is limited to the stated low degrees, bad-prime formulas remain essential, and formal Mobius cancellation without uniform bounds cannot transfer continuation.

title: Explicit-formula kernels separate uniform sign criteria from data-tuned certification
claim: An explicit formula can turn inaccessible zero information into a quadratic sign obligation or a residual term, and kernel design determines which arithmetic data are emphasized; demanding one sign for every admissible test function is categorically stronger than tuning a kernel to known small prime ideals for a finite explicit bound.
historical_or_program_relation: The RH positivity/negativity criterion presents test functions as a uniform structural probe modeled on geometric intersection signs, while discriminant computations use local arithmetic knowledge to choose data-adaptive kernels and infer an otherwise inaccessible zero contribution by subtraction.
limits: A successful data-tuned kernel does not establish uniform negativity, and the finite-field intersection sign does not identify or prove the missing classical quadratic representation; residual computation is valid only with fixed identity and kernel conventions.

title: Theta moments re-encode zero geometry as coefficient geometry
claim: Theta-transform representations convert completed-zeta derivatives into moments: one route amplifies an eventual sign of Xi into rigid derivative signs, while another packages central Taylor coefficients into Jensen polynomials whose hyperbolicity tests finite coefficient windows and whose eventual behavior follows from uniform saddle-point ratio asymptotics.
historical_or_program_relation: The classical Fourier/moment sign-change strategy and the modern Jensen-polynomial criterion use the same positive-moment access to completed-zeta coefficients but apply different finite-dimensional probes to the zero problem.
limits: The recovered classical span stops before its intended contradiction, and eventual Jensen hyperbolicity at each fixed degree is weaker than hyperbolicity for every degree and shift required by the RH equivalence; pointwise coefficient asymptotics without uniform local ratio control are insufficient.

title: Prime powers change status when the averaging symmetry changes
claim: Prime squares can be a lower-order error in a height-averaged zeta tail, a positive mean shift in a quadratic character family, and the natural signal in a prime-power density reconstructed from zeros; whether they may be removed is therefore determined by the averaging and target representation, not by exponent alone.
historical_or_program_relation: Moment methods use time or character orthogonality to decide which prime powers survive on the diagonal, while explicit-formula reconstruction deliberately stops before Mobius inversion so that the directly produced prime-power signal is retained.
limits: The negligibility statement uses its stated RH-dependent estimates, the quadratic-family shift uses a different averaging ensemble, and neither conclusion transfers unchanged to raw prime counts or to other symmetry families.

title: Moment proofs isolate a factorable diagonal and transform the off diagonal
claim: Zeta mean-value arguments separate multiplicative equality into a residue or Ramanujan-type main term, while unequal products are reindexed by differences and then converted through Poisson/Voronoi, Vaughan-Kloosterman, or automorphic spectral transforms into structures with usable cancellation.
historical_or_program_relation: The mollified second-moment analysis uses scale-adapted bilinear Kloosterman estimates, the mean-square formula uses an analytically continued difference-indexed series, and the fourth moment replaces one-dimensional transforms by an SL(2,Z) spectral decomposition whose Maass channel survives the final asymptotic scale selection.
limits: No single off-diagonal estimate covers every range, isolating a main term does not bound the remainders, and these smoothed moment mechanisms do not directly locate individual zeta zeros or prove RH.

title: Auxiliary variables make singular cancellation visible before specialization
claim: Introducing several complex variables creates a safe convergence domain in which an identity and its functional symmetries can be built; explicit residue extraction then continues the aggregate object, after which one may specialize to a fourth moment or read a family mean from a pole.
historical_or_program_relation: The four-variable fourth-moment formula and corrected multiple Dirichlet series share an order-of-operations discipline: regularize first, continue the whole coupled representation, and only then approach the singular target where separately divergent pieces can cancel.
limits: The fourth-moment identity and the family-moment program are different objects; in the latter, reaching and controlling the averaging pole plus Tauberian hypotheses remain genuine burdens, and a formal specialization before continuation is not licensed by aggregate cancellation.

title: Short zeta-sum bounds depend on adapters between theorem and application geometry
claim: After zeta is reduced to short exponential sums, useful cancellation requires explicit interface changes: Taylor polynomialization and mean-value duplication, periodic domain enlargement for decoupling, bilinear-to-linear interval recursion, Weyl shift correlations, scale-adapted blocks, and Abel summation back to the weighted Dirichlet polynomial.
historical_or_program_relation: Classical derivative and Weyl-differencing estimates, Vinogradov mean-value assembly, and modern decoupling improve different bottlenecks in the same reduction chain; parameter and range splicing record where each adapter is quantitatively compatible with the zeta application.
limits: The methods have different hypotheses and dominant ranges and cannot be combined by retaining only their best exponents; local cancellation bounds still require weighted transfer and global contour steps, and the resulting zero-free or zeta bounds remain weaker than RH.

title: Slow asymptotics make persistent finite behavior an unreliable guide
claim: Iterated-logarithmic growth, zero-driven oscillations, and ill-conditioned finite truncations give three mechanisms by which a correct asymptotic or pointwise limit can remain invisible or look qualitatively false throughout feasible computation.
historical_or_program_relation: The eventual reversal of a long-observed prime-counting bias supplies an arithmetic example, while slowly diverging model functions and a q-zeta approximation near a zero show the broader mismatch between theorem-scale convergence and finite numerical behavior.
limits: These examples do not locate the first prime-bias reversal, prove typical dominance at all large scales, give a general condition number for q-zeta truncations, or license skepticism about a finite computation that has an independent rigorous error certificate.

title: Contour zero counts serve different goals after the auxiliary object changes
claim: The argument principle can support a finite exhaustive RH certificate by comparing a total count with line witnesses, or an asymptotic lower proportion by replacing direct line zeros with zeros of a mollified differential combination and then bounding that auxiliary count through a mean square optimized variationally.
historical_or_program_relation: The same contour-counting resource moves from computational cardinality matching to Levinson-Conrey's analytic reduction, where representation freedom in the mollifier and differential combination trades individual certification for an optimizable global proportion.
limits: The two conclusions are not interchangeable: the mollified chain uses auxiliary zeros, shifted contours, and differing multiplicity conventions, its variational optimizer must be returned to the admissible polynomial class, and a positive proportion is neither finite completeness nor RH.

title: Symmetry can project zeta-value identities onto parity-restricted families
claim: Parity restrictions can be engineered before evaluation: real and imaginary parts of a contour representation select different parity-indexed log-sine moments, while a symmetric rational function makes partial fractions and integer summation produce linear forms supported only on odd zeta values.
historical_or_program_relation: Integral identities and irrationality constructions use different auxiliary objects but share a representation-level projection move that replaces accidental cancellation at the end with symmetry-controlled support from the start.
limits: The damaged integral formulas support only the proof architecture, not coefficient-level identities or a single verified projector common to the even and odd cases; the rational-function construction additionally needs denominator control and analytic smallness, and neither special-value mechanism bears directly on RH zero location.
